source.title: SafeInfer: Context Adaptive Decoding Time Safety Alignment for Large Language Models
source.authors: Somnath Banerjee; Soham Tripathy; Sayan Layek; Shanu Kumar; Animesh Mukherjee; Rima Hazra

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. It includes some PDF extraction artifacts, but the results relevant here are readable.
record.tranche_reason: It tests whether jailbreak attacks lead a safety-aligned chat model to produce harmful responses, using attack-success rates rather than the original studies’ fine-tuning or token-position measurements.
record.gate_note: Table 4 reports harmful-response rates for Llama-2 under five jailbreak methods on two datasets; those attack-condition outcomes are recorded. The paper also reports SafeDecoding and SafeInfer rates in Table 4, but these are comparisons of decoding defenses rather than additional tests of the attack effect. The study does not measure KL divergence by response position, compliant-prefix prefilling, fine-tuning safety erosion, or safety localization.
record.test_reason: This is a decoding-time defense paper (SafeInfer). Its only result bearing on a version is the undefended Llama-2-7b-chat attack success rate (ASR) under GCG adversarial suffixes (Table 4). Read against the same model's no-attack ASR in Table 1, GCG raises harmful responses but leaves most refused. The other four jailbreaks are whole-prompt rewrites, not prefills, suffixes or decoding changes. The defense results are mitigation comparisons, not tests of the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude SafeInfer gives the lowest harmful ASR across models, datasets, prompt types and jailbreaks while preserving utility (MMLU, TruthfulQA, ARC, GSM8K). Over-safety on XSTest rises only slightly (17.83→20.09 on Llama-2), unlike SafeDecoding (80.3).
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates jailbreak attacks and a decoding-time safety defense; it does not reproduce the original fine-tuning or token-position measurement procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports different ASRs across jailbreak methods and datasets, and across simple, instruction-centric, and instruction-centric CoT prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: Prompt-level jailbreaks (AutoDAN, PAIR, DeepInception, GPTFuzzer) raise Llama-2-7b-chat harmful ASR to 0.29–0.68, versus about 20–22% with no attack.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whole-prompt jailbreaks raise harmful compliance of safety-aligned chat models.

fits_no_version.finding: Instruction-centric code-style prompts raise Llama-2 ASR on TechHazardQA from 43.00% (simple prompt) to 86.85%, and to 89.14% with CoT (Tables 1 and 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reframing harmful requests as code-writing tasks bypasses refusal.

fits_no_version.finding: ROME knowledge editing of Llama-2 changes harmful ASR inconsistently. It rises on NicheHazardQA (31.55→43.55), HarmEval (12.73→18.18) and TechHazardQA instruction prompts (86.15→88.29). It falls on DangerousQA (12.5→8), AdvBench (20→13.08) and HEx-PHI (49.09→24.45) (Table 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model editing alters safety behaviour of aligned models.

record.problems: For the attack-rate results relevant here, the reported tests use Llama-2 only; uncertainty estimates are not stated. The paper does not report a matched no-attack condition in Table 4.
record.rows_left_out: SafeDecoding and SafeInfer values in Table 4 are defense-comparison results and were not extracted as separate rows. Other ASR tables evaluate the proposed safety method under ordinary or instruction-based prompts, rather than testing the attack-bypass behaviour captured by V4.

untested.parts: A harmful model (about 100 harmful QA pairs, full fine-tune of the same family) is built as a tool for the defense, but its harmful-compliance rate is never reported.
Benign fine-tuning is not tested. ROME knowledge editing is not fine-tuning on benign data.
No per-position KL divergence between aligned and base models.
Compliant-prefix prefilling and decoding-parameter changes as bypasses are not tested. Only GCG suffixes bear on V4; transfer and optimization details of the GCG suffixes are not stated.
Not tested. The attention-head selection is used only to build a steering vector.
Not tested. SafeInfer is a decoding-time intervention, not training that deepens alignment.

missing.what: No-attack ASR for undefended Llama-2: AdvBench 20.00%, HarmEval 21.63%. This is the baseline needed for the GCG rows.

record.verdict_notes: Judging is by GPT-4 with a broad 'ethical concerns' criterion, checked against humans on a 40% sample (>93% agreement). This may explain the unusually high no-attack ASR for Llama-2-chat. The study reports no uncertainty. Whether the GCG suffixes were optimized on this model is not stated. The Figure 2 illustration of the harmful fine-tuned model favouring 'Sure' at 98% is a schematic, not a measured result.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether fine-tuning a safety-trained model on harmful examples removes refusal.
Does not test whether ordinary or carefully chosen benign fine-tuning data raises harmful compliance.
Does not measure per-token KL divergence or its distribution across response positions.
Tests jailbreak methods, including GCG, but does not test compliant-token prefilling or decoding changes as bypasses.
Does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Does not test whether the training data or objective causes safety to be shallow.
Does not test training that spreads safety beyond initial response tokens or whether such training holds up.

relationships.condition: Llama-2-7b-chat, GCG suffix attack, AdvBench and HarmEval, GPT-4 ethics judge
relationships.reason: GCG roughly doubles harmful responses over no attack (20%→37%, 21.6%→48%) but most or half of requests are still refused (R1, R6).
relationships.display_finding: Harmful responses rose from 20% to 37% on AdvBench and from 21.6% to 48% on HarmEval, so half or more of requests were still refused.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.condition: Llama-2 under the five tested jailbreak methods on AdvBench and HarmEval
reader_labels.reason: The attacks yield measurable but incomplete harmful-response ASRs, ranging from 0.29 to 0.68; these results do not test compliant-prefix prefilling or decoding changes as bypasses (R1–R10).
